description:
Marian Hossa joined the Detroit Red Wings in July 2008, bringing his elite scoring ability to a team hungry for another Stanley Cup. On October 24, 2008, he put on a show against his former team, the Atlanta Thrashers, scoring two goals and adding an assist in a 5–3 win at Joe Louis Arena. Hossa finished the season with 40 goals and 31 assists in 74 games, playing a key role in the Red Wings’ success. The next year, he signed with Chicago and went on to win three Stanley Cups.

description:
Gordie Howe capped off his legendary NHL career with the Hartford Whalers during the 1979–80 season, playing all 80 games and finishing with 15 goals and 41 points.  On April 9, 1980, in Game 2 of the Preliminary Round against the Montreal Canadiens, the 52-year-old Howe scored the final playoff goal of his NHL career on a backhand from the top of the left circle after taking a pass from his son Mark. The goal came late in the third period of an 8–4 loss and drew a standing ovation from the Montreal crowd in recognition of one of hockey’s all-time greats.

description:
Marc-Andre Fleury joined the Chicago Blackhawks in July 2021, bringing championship experience and steady leadership to a team in transition. On February 18, 2022, Fleury stood tall against the Dallas Stars, stopping all 29 shots in a hard-fought 1–0 shootout loss at the United Center. One of his standout moments came in the final seconds of the second period, when he made an incredible glove save to deny Roope Hintz all alone in front of the net. Despite the loss, his performance was a clear reminder of why he was one of the league’s most dependable goaltenders throughout his career. Fleury appeared in 45 games that season before being traded to the Minnesota Wild in March 2022.
